events.text: The Temple of Juno Regina (Aventine) is dedicated in Rome by Marcus Furius Camillus.
Byzantine general Isaak Komnenos is crowned Byzantine Emperor by patriarch Cerularius at the Hagia Sophia.
The main altar of Lund Cathedral, then the Catholic cathedral of all the Nordic countries, was dedicated to Saint Lawrence and the Virgin Mary.
The main altar of Lund Cathedral, at the time the seat of the archiepiscopal see of all the Nordic countries, is consecrated.
The widow Stamira sacrifices herself in order to raise the siege of Ancona by the forces of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa.

main.desc: Legendary figure who saved the Italian city of Ancona from invasion in 1173

events.text: Election of pope Lucius III following the death of pope Alexander III in the previous month.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1181 to 1185

events.text: Election of pope Gregory X following the death of Clement IV three years prior.

main.desc: Election of Catholic Pope Gregory X

events.text: King Tvrtko I of Bosnia writes In castro nostro Vizoka vocatum from the Old town of Visoki.

main.desc: First king of Bosnia from 1377 to 1391

events.text: Tumu Crisis: The Mongols capture the Emperor of China.
The Spanish fort of Sancti Spiritu, the first one built in modern Argentina, is destroyed by indigenous people.

main.desc: Settlement established by Sebastian Cabot in 1527

events.text: Lady Anne Boleyn is made Marquess of Pembroke by her fiancé, King Henry VIII of England.
The Guru Granth Sahib (folio depicted), the religious text of Sikhism, was installed in the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
Adi Granth, now known as Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture of Sikhs, is first installed at Harmandir Sahib.
Claudio Monteverdi's Vespro della Beata Vergine (page pictured) was first printed in Venice, dedicated to Pope Paul V.
Claudio Monteverdi's musical work Vespro della Beata Vergine (Vespers for the Blessed Virgin) is first published, printed in Venice and dedicated to Pope Paul V.
Battle of Tippermuir: James Graham, 1st Marquess of Montrose defeats the Earl of Wemyss's Covenanters, reviving the Royalist cause.

main.desc: Part of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms

events.text: English Civil War: Scottish Covenanter forces abandon their month-long Siege of Hereford, a Cavalier stronghold, on news of Royalist victories in Scotland.
At the age of five, Louis XV becomes king of France in succession to his great-grandfather, King Louis XIV.
Catherine the Great, Empress of Russia, endorses Ivan Betskoy's plans for a Foundling Home in Moscow.
The Mission San Luis Obispo de Tolosa is founded in San Luis Obispo, California.

main.t: Mission San Luis Obispo de Tolosa

events.text: Under orders from Governor Thomas Gage, British soldiers removed gunpowder from a magazine in the Province of Massachusetts Bay, which caused Patriots to prepare for war.

main.desc: British Army officer and colonial administrator (1718/19–1787)

events.text: Massachusetts Bay colonists rise up in the bloodless Powder Alarm.

main.desc: British colony in North America from 1691 to 1776

events.text: German astronomer Karl Ludwig Harding discovered one of the largest main-belt asteroids, naming it Juno after the Roman goddess.
3 Juno, one of the largest asteroids in the Main Belt, is discovered by the German astronomer Karl Ludwig Harding.

The Order of St. Gregory the Great is established by Pope Gregory XVI of the Vatican State to recognize high support for the Vatican or for the Pope, by a man or a woman, and not necessarily a Roman Catholic.

main.t: Order of St. Gregory the Great
main.desc: Papal Order of Knighthood of the Holy See

events.text: Narcissa Whitman, one of the first English-speaking white women to settle west of the Rocky Mountains, arrives at Walla Walla, Washington.
Saint Andrew's Scots School, the oldest school of British origin in South America, is established.

main.desc: School in Olivos, Vicente López Partido, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina

events.text: A powerful solar flare caused a coronal mass ejection that struck Earth a few hours later, generating the most intense geomagnetic storm ever recorded and causing bright aurorae visible in the middle latitudes.
Carrington Event started - the most intense geomagnetic storm in recorded history.
American Civil War: Confederate forces attacked retreating troops (map shown) of the Union army during a rainstorm in Chantilly, Virginia, but the battle ended inconclusively.
American Civil War: Confederate forces under General Stonewall Jackson inflict heavy casualties in the Battle of Chantilly during the Union withdrawal from the Northern Virginia campaign.

American Civil War: The Battle of Jonesborough, alongside the overall Atlanta campaign, culminates in a Union victory for General William T. Sherman as Confederate General John Bell Hood orders the evacuation of Atlanta.

main.desc: 1864 battle of the American Civil War

events.text: Franco-Prussian War: The Battle of Sedan is fought, resulting in a decisive Prussian victory.
A small British force commanded by a surgeon fought off a surprise attack by the Maya on Orange Walk Town, British Honduras.
Cetshwayo ascends to the throne as king of the Zulu nation following the death of his father Mpande.
Emma Nutt becomes the world's first female telephone operator when she is recruited by Alexander Graham Bell to the Boston Telephone Dispatch Company.
The army of Mohammad Ayub Khan is routed by the British at the Battle of Kandahar, ending the Second Anglo-Afghan War.
Over 400 people die in the Great Hinckley Fire, a forest fire in Hinckley, Minnesota.
The Tremont Street Subway in Boston opens, becoming the first underground rapid transit system in North America.
The first science fiction film, titled A Trip to the Moon and based on From the Earth to the Moon by Jules Verne, was released in France.

links.t: From the Earth to the Moon

events.text: Construction began on the Saline Valley salt tram, which during its operation was the steepest tram in the United States.
The passenger pigeon, which once numbered in the billions, became extinct when the last individual died in captivity.
The Great Kantō Earthquake devastates Tokyo and Yokohama, killing about 105,000 people.
The first group of around 172,000 Koreans were deported by Soviet authorities from the Russian Far East to the Kazakh and Uzbek SSRs; around 10 to 25 percent died.

main.desc: Ethnic Koreans in the former USSR

links.t: Deportation of Koreans in the Soviet Union

events.text: German forces attacked multiple locations in Poland, including Wieluń and Westerplatte, starting World War II in Europe.

main.desc: Invasion at the beginning of World War II

links.t: European theatre of World War II

events.text: World War II: Germany and Slovakia invade Poland, beginning the European phase of World War II.
J. Robert Oppenheimer and his student Hartland Snyder publish the Oppenheimer–Snyder model, proving for the first time in contemporary physics how black holes could develop.
World War II: Launch of Operation Ratweek, complicating German retreat.
Ernest Hemingway's novel The Old Man and the Sea, which later won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, was first published.

links.t: The Old Man and the Sea

events.text: TWA Flight 529 crashes shortly after takeoff from Midway Airport in Chicago, killing all 78 people on board. At the time, it was the deadliest single plane disaster in U.S. history.
Rioting erupted in Dayton, Ohio, resulting in one death and the mobilization of the Ohio National Guard.
At an Arab League summit, eight nations issued the Khartoum Resolution, declaring that there would be "no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, [and] no negotiations with it".
Six-Day War: The Khartoum Resolution is issued at the Arab Summit, and eight countries adopt the "three 'no's against Israel".

main.desc: 1967 war between Israel and Arab states

events.text: Muammar Gaddafi (pictured) led a coup d'état to overthrow King Idris of Libya.
A coup in Libya brings Muammar Gaddafi to power.

main.desc: Coup d'état by the Free Officers movement

events.text: In a match widely publicized as a Cold War confrontation, American chess grandmaster Bobby Fischer became the 11th World Chess Champion with his victory over Soviet Boris Spassky.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: A 76-hour multinational rescue effort off the coast of Ireland resulted in the deepest sub rescue in history.

main.t: Rescue of Roger Mallinson and Roger Chapman

events.text: A 76-hour multinational rescue effort in the Celtic Sea results in the rescue of Roger Mallinson and Roger Chapman.

links.t: Rescue of Roger Mallinson and Roger Chapman

events.text: The SR-71 Blackbird sets (and holds) the record for flying from New York to London in the time of one hour, 54 minutes and 56.4 seconds at a speed of 1,435.587 miles per hour (2,310.353 km/h).
Central African President David Dacko is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by General André Kolingba.

main.desc: President of the Central African Republic (1960–1965, 1979–1981)

events.text: The United States Air Force Space Command is founded.

main.t: United States Space Force Combat Forces Command

events.text: Cold War: Korean Air Lines Flight 007 is shot down by a Soviet jet fighter after the commercial aircraft strayed into Soviet airspace, killing all 269 on board, including Congressman Lawrence McDonald.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: The wreck of the Titanic is discovered by an American-French expedition led by Robert Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel.

main.desc: British passenger liner that sank in 1912

events.text: Speakers' Corner, a free speech area in Hong Lim Park in Singapore, was launched.

The Beslan school siege begins when armed terrorists take schoolchildren and school staff hostage in North Ossetia, Russia; by the end of the siege, three days later, more than 385 people are dead (including hostages, other civilians, security personnel and terrorists).
Iraq War: The United States Armed Forces transfers control of Anbar Province to the Iraqi Armed Forces.
Pharaoh Cleopatra VII of Egypt declares her son co-ruler as Ptolemy XV Caesarion.
Cicero launches the first of his Philippicae (oratorical attacks) on Mark Antony. He will make 14 of them over the following months.
Final War of the Roman Republic: Battle of Actium: Off the western coast of Greece, forces of Octavian defeat troops under Mark Antony and Cleopatra.

main.desc: War between Mark Antony and Octavian, 32–30 BC

events.text: The Byzantine Empire and the Kievan Rus sign a treaty regulating trade.
The Treaty of Jaffa is signed between Richard I of England and Saladin, leading to the end of the Third Crusade.
Entry of Mary, Queen of Scots into Edinburgh, a spectacular civic celebration for the Queen of Scotland, marred by religious controversy.

main.t: Entry of Mary, Queen of Scots, into Edinburgh
main.desc: 1561 royal entry celebration for Mary, Queen of Scots in Edinburgh

events.text: An imperial army retakes the city of Esztergom from the Ottoman Empire.

main.t: Army of the Holy Roman Empire
main.desc: Armed forces of the Holy Roman Empire

events.text: 4th Spanish Armada makes landfall in Ireland at Kinsale.
The Italian city of Castro is completely destroyed by the forces of Pope Innocent X, ending the Wars of Castro.

main.desc: Ancient city in Ischia di Castro, northern Lazio, Italy

events.text: A large fire began in London's Pudding Lane and burned for five days,  destroying St Paul's Cathedral and the homes of 70,000 of the city's 80,000 inhabitants.
The Great Fire of London breaks out and burns for three days, destroying 10,000 buildings, including Old St Paul's Cathedral.
Great Britain, along with its overseas possessions, adopts the Gregorian calendar.
The United States Department of the Treasury was founded following financial concerns in the new nation.

main.t: United States Department of the Treasury

events.text: The United States Department of the Treasury is founded.

main.t: United States Department of the Treasury

events.text: French Revolution: Due to an overwhelming fear that foreign armies would attack Paris and prisoners would revolt, revolutionaries began the summary execution of more than a thousand prisoners.

During what became known as the September Massacres of the French Revolution, rampaging mobs slaughter three Roman Catholic bishops, more than two hundred priests, and prisoners believed to be royalist sympathizers.
A massive landslide destroys the town of Goldau, Switzerland, killing 457.

main.desc: City in the community of Arth, canton of Schwyz, Switzerland

events.text: Napoleonic Wars: The British Royal Navy bombards Copenhagen with fire bombs and phosphorus rockets to prevent Denmark from surrendering its fleet to Napoleon.
The Tianjing incident takes place in Nanjing, China.

main.desc: 1856 internal conflict in the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom

events.text: The Carrington Event is the strongest geomagnetic storm on record.

American Civil War: United States President Abraham Lincoln reluctantly restores Union General George B. McClellan to full command after General John Pope's disastrous defeat at the Second Battle of Bull Run.
American Civil War: Union forces enter Atlanta as the city surrenders, ending the Atlanta campaign as a victory for General William T. Sherman.
Mutsuhito, Emperor Meiji of Japan, marries Masako Ichijō, thereafter known as Empress Shōken.
Franco-Prussian War: Prussian forces captured Napoleon III at the Battle of Sedan, which led to the collapse of the Second French Empire within days.
Franco-Prussian War: Battle of Sedan: Prussian forces take Napoleon III of France and 100,000 of his soldiers prisoner.
White miners in Rock Springs, Wyoming, attacked Chinese-American immigrants, killing at least 28 Chinese miners and causing approximately $150,000 in property damage.

main.desc: City in Sweetwater County, Wyoming, US

events.text: Rock Springs massacre: In Rock Springs, Wyoming, 150 white miners, who are struggling to unionize so they could strike for better wages and work conditions, attack their Chinese fellow workers, killing 28, wounding 15 and forcing several hundred more out of town.
Battle of Omdurman: British and Egyptian troops defeat Sudanese tribesmen and establish British dominance in Sudan.

U.S. vice president Theodore Roosevelt first publicly used the phrase "speak softly and carry a big stick" (cartoon pictured) at the Minnesota State Fair, describing his philosophy of negotiating peacefully while simultaneously threatening to use military force.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1901 to 1909

events.text: Vice President of the United States Theodore Roosevelt utters the famous phrase, "Speak softly and carry a big stick" at the Minnesota State Fair.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1901 to 1909

events.text: Arthur Rose Eldred became the first person to attain the rank of Eagle Scout in the Boy Scouts of America.

main.desc: First Eagle Scout in the United States

events.text: Arthur Rose Eldred is awarded the first Eagle Scout award of the Boy Scouts of America.

main.desc: First Eagle Scout in the United States

events.text: Kantō Massacre: Amid rumors that Koreans had been conducting acts of sabotage in the aftermath of the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake, lynch mobs of Japanese begin massacring thousands of civilians over the course of several weeks, mainly ethnic minorities such as Koreans and Chinese.
The Labor Day Hurricane, the most intense hurricane to strike the United States, makes landfall at Long Key, Florida, killing at least 400.
World War II: Following the start of the invasion of Poland the previous day, the Free City of Danzig (now Gdańsk, Poland) is annexed by Nazi Germany.
The last execution of a Finn in Finland takes place when soldier Olavi Laiho is executed by shooting in Oulu.

On the deck of the U.S. Navy battleship Missouri in Tokyo Bay, representatives from the Empire of Japan and the Allied powers signed the Japanese Instrument of Surrender , formally ending World War II.

main.desc: Maritime service branch of the U.S. military

events.text: World War II: The Japanese Instrument of Surrender is signed by Japan and the major warring powers aboard the battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, thus marking the official end to the war.
Communist leader Ho Chi Minh proclaims the Democratic Republic of Vietnam after the end of the Nguyễn dynasty.

main.desc: Leader of North Vietnam from 1945 to 1969

links.t: Declaration of independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam

events.text: The interim government of India, headed by Jawaharlal Nehru, was formed to assist the transition of India from British rule to independence.
The Interim Government of India is formed, headed by Jawaharlal Nehru as vice president with the powers of a Prime Minister.
South Vietnamese president Ngô Đình Diệm began an official visit to Australia, the first by a foreign incumbent head of state to the country.

links.t: Ngo Dinh Diem presidential visit to Australia

events.text: President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam becomes the first foreign head of state to make a state visit to Australia.

main.desc: President of South Vietnam from 1955 to 1963

links.t: Ngo Dinh Diem presidential visit to Australia

events.text: A USAF RC-130 is shot down by fighters over Armenia when it strays into Soviet airspace while conducting a sigint mission. All crew members are killed.

main.desc: Military reconnaissance aircraft mainly used in the U.S. Air Force

events.text: The first election of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile. The Tibetan community observes this date as Democracy Day.

main.t: Parliament of the Central Tibetan Administration
main.desc: Unicameral legislature of the government-in-exile of Tibet

events.text: CBS Evening News becomes U.S. network television's first half-hour weeknight news broadcast, when the show is lengthened from 15 to 30 minutes.

Paddy Roy Bates proclaimed HM Fort Roughs, a former World War II Maunsell Sea Fort in the North Sea off the coast of Suffolk, England, as an independent sovereign state: the Principality of Sealand (pictured).
Operation OAU begins during the Nigerian Civil War.
NASA announces the cancellation of two Apollo missions to the Moon, Apollo 15 (the designation is re-used by a later mission), and Apollo 19.

Aeroflot Flight 3630, a Tupolev Tu-124 en route from southern Russia to Lithuania, crashes after the pilots lost control of the aircraft at cruise altitude between Rostov-on-Don Airport and Vilnius Airport, on the second leg of the flight; all 37 passengers and crew are killed.
Seven people are shot and killed and 12 wounded in the Milperra massacre, a shootout between the rival motorcycle gangs Bandidos and Comancheros in Sydney, Australia.

Hurricane Elena, an unpredictable and damaging tropical cyclone that affected eastern and central portions of the United States Gulf Coast, made landfall near Biloxi, Mississippi, as a Category 3 major hurricane.

links.t: Gulf Coast of the United States

events.text: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Tamil politicians and former MPs M. Alalasundaram and V. Dharmalingam are shot dead.
In Moscow, the trial begins for 19-year-old pilot Mathias Rust, who flew his Cessna airplane into Red Square in May.

main.desc: German activist, landed a plane near Red Square in Moscow in 1987

events.text: Transnistria is unilaterally proclaimed a Soviet republic; the Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev declares the decision null and void.

links.t: Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union

events.text: An earthquake registering 7.7 Mw off the coast of Nicaragua became the first tsunami earthquake to be captured on modern broadband seismic networks.

main.desc: Earthquake and tsunami off the west coast of Nicaragua

events.text: The 7.7 Mw Nicaragua earthquake affects the west coast of Nicaragua. With a Ms–Mw disparity of half a unit, this tsunami earthquake triggers a tsunami that causes most of the damage and casualties, with at least 116 killed. Typical runup heights were 3–8 meters (9.8–26.2 ft).

main.desc: Earthquake and tsunami off the west coast of Nicaragua

events.text: A fire in the cockpit on Swissair Flight 111, en route from New York City to Geneva, caused the aircraft to crash into the Atlantic Ocean near Canada, killing all 229 people on board.
Swissair Flight 111 crashes near Peggy's Cove, Nova Scotia; all 229 people on board are killed.
The UN's International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda finds Jean-Paul Akayesu, the former mayor of a small town in Rwanda, guilty of nine counts of genocide.
Google launches its Google Chrome web browser.

The Andhra Pradesh, India helicopter crash occurs near Rudrakonda Hill, 40 nautical miles (74 km) from Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, India. Fatalities include Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy, the Chief Minister of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
Israel-Palestinian conflict: the 2010 Israeli-Palestinian peace talks are launched by the United States.

main.desc: Ongoing military and political conflict in West Asia

events.text: Bad weather caused a Chilean Air Force aircraft to crash into the Pacific Ocean, killing all 21 people on board.

main.desc: Air warfare branch of Chile's armed forces

events.text: The Eastern span replacement of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge opens at 10:15 pm at a cost of $6.4 billion, after the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake damaged the old span.

main.t: Eastern span replacement of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge

events.text: National Museum of Brazil fire: A massive fire destroys most of the Paço de São Cristóvão, which houses the National Museum of Brazil, in Rio de Janeiro. The museum holds important archaeοlogical and anthropological objects, including the remains of the Luzia Woman, Marajoara vases and Egyptian mummies.

main.desc: 2018 museum fire at Rio de Janeiro

events.text: Hurricane Dorian, a category 5 hurricane, devastates the Bahamas, killing at least five.
The dive boat MV Conception catches fire and sinks near Santa Cruz Island, killing 34.
Eighteen people are killed and 23 others are injured by a suicide bombing at a Sunni mosque in Herat, Afghanistan.
India's first solar observation mission: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launches Aditya-L1 from Satish Dhawan space centre.
Four people are killed in a mass shooting targeting homeless people on a Chicago Transit Authority train in Forest Park, Illinois, United States.

main.desc: Rapid transit system in Chicago, Illinois

events.text: A suicide bombing in Kabul, Afghanistan, kills six people and injures 13.
At least 129 inmates are killed and 59 more injured in an attempted prison break at Makala Prison in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

main.desc: 2024 attempted jailbreak at the Makala Central Prison

events.text: The Sicilian revolt against the Second Triumvirate of the Roman Republic ended when the fleet of Sextus Pompey, the rebel leader, was defeated at the Battle of Naulochus.

main.t: War between Sextus Pompey and the Second Triumvirate
main.desc: Civil war in the Roman Republic (42–36 BC)

events.text: In the Battle of Naulochus, Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, admiral of Octavian, defeats Sextus Pompey, son of Pompey, thus ending Pompeian resistance to the Second Triumvirate.
San Marino, one of the smallest nations in the world and the world's oldest republic still in existence, is founded by Saint Marinus.

links.t: List of countries and dependencies by area

events.text: Consecration of Pope Gregory I (Gregory the Great).

main.desc: 64th Bishop of Rome; head of the Roman Catholic Church from AD 590 to 604

events.text: King Wamba of the Visigoths puts down a revolt by Hilderic, governor of Nîmes (France) and rival for the throne.

main.desc: King of the Visigoths from 672 to 680

events.text: Arab–Byzantine wars: The Byzantine Empire decisively defeated the Emirate of Melitene at the Battle of Lalakaon, beginning the era of Byzantine ascendancy.

main.desc: Series of wars between the 7th and 11th centuries

links.t: Byzantine Empire under the Macedonian dynasty

events.text: Major Byzantine victory under general Petronas at the Battle of Lalakaon against an Arab raid under emir Umar al-Aqta, who is killed in battle.
Richard I of England (a.k.a. Richard "the Lionheart") is crowned at Westminster.
The Mamluks defeat the Mongols at the Battle of Ain Jalut in Palestine, marking their first decisive defeat and the point of maximum expansion of the Mongol Empire.

main.desc: Slave-soldiers and enslaved mercenaries in the Muslim world

events.text: At the congress of Visegrád Charles I of Hungary mediates a reconciliation between two neighboring monarchs, John of Bohemia and Casimir III of Poland.

main.desc: King of Hungary and Croatia from 1308 to 1342

events.text: The Treaty of Selymbria was concluded between the Republic of Venice and the Ottoman prince Musa Çelebi.
The Treaty of Selymbria is concluded between the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Venice.
Under Oliver Cromwell, the English New Model Army ambushed a poorly prepared Scottish force at the Battle of Dunbar, the first battle of the Third English Civil War.
Victory over the royalists in the Battle of Dunbar opens the way to Edinburgh for the New Model Army during the English invasion of Scotland.

English Parliamentarian forces under Oliver Cromwell (pictured) won the Battle of Worcester, the final battle of the English Civil War.* 1777 – American Revolutionary War: The British Army and their Hessian allies defeated an American militia at the Battle of Cooch's Bridge.

main.desc: Parliament supporter in the English Civil War

events.text: The Battle of Worcester is the last significant action in the Wars of the Three Kingdoms.

main.desc: 1651 final battle of the English Civil War

events.text: The death of Oliver Cromwell; Richard Cromwell becomes Lord Protector of England.
The Royal Exchange burns down in the Great Fire of London.
American Revolutionary War: During the Battle of Cooch's Bridge, the Flag of the United States is flown in battle for the first time.
American Revolutionary War: The war ends with the signing of the Treaty of Paris by the United States and the Kingdom of Great Britain.

main.desc: Agreement ending the American Revolutionary War

events.text: The week long battle of St. George's Caye begins between Spain and Britain off the coast of Belize.

main.desc: 1798 attempted Spanish invasion of British Honduras during the French Revolutionary Wars

events.text: Twenty-four settlers are killed in the Pigeon Roost Massacre in Indiana.

main.desc: Site of an 1812 massacre of settlers by Native Americans in Indiana, United States

events.text: Future abolitionist Frederick Douglass escapes from slavery.
King Otto of Greece is forced to grant a constitution following an uprising in Athens.
American Indian Wars: In Nebraska, 700 soldiers under United States General William S. Harney avenge the Grattan massacre by attacking a Sioux village and killing 100 men, women and children.

main.desc: Frontier conflicts in the United States, 1609–1890s

events.text: American Civil War: Confederate General Leonidas Polk invades neutral Kentucky, prompting the state legislature to ask for Union assistance.

links.t: Kentucky in the American Civil War

events.text: Franco-Prussian War: The Siege of Metz begins, resulting in a decisive Prussian victory on October 23.
The passenger steamship SS Princess Alice sank in the River Thames after colliding (pictured) with the collier Bywell Castle, killing more than 600 people.
Over 640 die when the crowded pleasure boat Princess Alice collides with the Bywell Castle in the River Thames.

Siege of the British Residency in Kabul: British envoy Sir Louis Cavagnari and 72 men of the Guides are massacred by Afghan troops while defending the British Residency in Kabul. Their heroism and loyalty became famous and revered throughout the British Empire.

main.t: Siege of the British Residency in Kabul
main.desc: 1879 battle of the Second Anglo-Afghan War

events.text: John Brallier becomes the first openly paid professional American football player, when he was paid US$10 by David Berry, to play for the Latrobe Athletic Association in a 12–0 win over the Jeanette Athletic Association.
At the Royal Exhibition Building (pictured) in Melbourne, the flag of Australia flew for the first time.

main.desc: Heritage building in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia

events.text: A fire that started on Fraser's Million Dollar Pier destroys six to eight square blocks of Ocean Park, California.
Wilhelm, Prince of Albania leaves the country after just six months due to opposition to his rule.
French composer Albéric Magnard is killed defending his estate against invading German soldiers.
World War I: Start of the Battle of Grand Couronné, a German assault against French positions on high ground near the city of Nancy.
World War I: Leefe Robinson destroys the German airship Schütte-Lanz SL 11 over Cuffley, north of London; this is the first German airship to be shot down on British soil.

USS Shenandoah, the United States' first American-built rigid airship, is destroyed in a squall line over Noble County, Ohio. Fourteen of her 42-man crew perished, including her commander, Zachary Lansdowne.

main.desc: United States Navy rigid airship destroyed in 1925

events.text: Yevgeniy Abalakov is the first man to reach the highest point in the Soviet Union, Communism Peak (now called Ismoil Somoni Peak and situated in Tajikistan) (7495 m).
On the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah, British racing motorist Malcolm Campbell (pictured) became the first person to drive an automobile over 300 mph (480 km/h).
Sir Malcolm Campbell reaches a speed of 304.331 miles per hour on the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah, becoming the first person to drive an automobile over 300 mph.

main.desc: British racing driver and speed record holder (1885–1948)

events.text: The Guild of Carillonneurs in North America was founded in Parliament Hill, Ottawa, Canada.

main.t: The Guild of Carillonneurs in North America

events.text: World War II: France, the United Kingdom, New Zealand and Australia declare war on Germany after the invasion of Poland, forming the Allied nations. The Viceroy of India also declares war, but without consulting the provincial legislatures.
World War II: The United Kingdom and France begin a naval blockade of Germany that lasts until the end of the war. This also marks the beginning of the Battle of the Atlantic.

main.desc: WWII operation to restrict supply lines

events.text: The mass expulsion of Soviet Germans from the Volga German ASSR began.

main.desc: Soviet forced displacement of ethnic Germans

links.t: Volga German Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic

events.text: The Holocaust: Karl Fritzsch, deputy camp commandant of the Auschwitz concentration camp, experiments with the use of Zyklon B in the gassing of Soviet POWs.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: The Holocaust: In possibly the first Jewish ghetto uprising, residents of the Łachwa Ghetto in occupied Poland, informed of the upcoming "liquidation" of the ghetto, unsuccessfully fought against their Nazi captors.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: World War II: In response to news of its coming liquidation, Dov Lopatyn leads an uprising in the Ghetto of Lakhva (present-day Belarus).

World War II: British and Canadian troops land on the Italian mainland. On the same day, Walter Bedell Smith and Giuseppe Castellano sign the Armistice of Cassibile, although it is not announced for another five days.

main.desc: 1943 Allied amphibious assault on Italy across the Straits of Messina

events.text: Holocaust: Diarist Anne Frank and her family are placed on the last transport train from the Westerbork transit camp to the Auschwitz concentration camp, arriving three days later.

main.desc: Record of events with entries arranged by date

events.text: A three-day celebration begins in China, following the Victory over Japan Day on September 2.

main.desc: Celebration of the end of World War II

events.text: "Nino" Farina becomes the first Formula One Drivers' champion after winning the 1950 Italian Grand Prix.

links.t: List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions

events.text: The People's Liberation Army begins shelling the Republic of China-controlled islands of Quemoy, starting the First Taiwan Strait Crisis.

main.desc: Combined military forces of the People's Republic of China

events.text: Dagen H in Sweden: Traffic changes from driving on the left to driving on the right overnight.

main.desc: 3 Sept 1967 in Sweden, when traffic changed from left- to right-hand

events.text: Qatar becomes an independent state.
Viking program: The American Viking 2 spacecraft lands at Utopia Planitia on Mars.

A group of hunters at the Stampede trail near Healy, Alaska come across a male corpse in abandoned bus, later identified as Christopher McCandless.
Cal Ripken Jr. (pictured) played his 2,131st consecutive Major League Baseball game, breaking the 56-year-old record set by Lou Gehrig.

links.t: List of Major League Baseball consecutive games played leaders

events.text: Cal Ripken Jr. of the Baltimore Orioles plays in his 2,131st consecutive game, breaking a record that had stood for 56 years.
An estimated 2.5 billion people worldwide watched the funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales, on television.

main.t: Funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales

events.text: The funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales takes place in London. Well over a million people line the streets and 21⁄2 billion watch around the world on television.

main.t: Funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales

events.text: Royal Brunei Airlines Flight 839 crashes in the Lambir Hills National Park while on approach to Miri Airport in Malaysia, killing 10.
The Parliament of Singapore relocated from the Old Parliament House to its current meeting place (pictured).
The Los Angeles Dodgers hosted the first Pride Night in Major League Baseball history.
Mahmoud Abbas resigns from his position of Palestinian Prime Minister.
Israel executes the air strike Operation Orchard to destroy a nuclear reactor in Syria.
The ro-ro ferry SuperFerry 9 sinks off the Zamboanga Peninsula in the Philippines with 971 persons aboard; all but ten are rescued.

main.desc: Vessels designed to carry wheeled cargo

events.text: Sixty-one people die after a fishing boat capsizes off the İzmir Province coast of Turkey, near the Greek Aegean islands.

main.t: September 2012 Baradan Bay, Turkey, migrant boat disaster

events.text: Forty-one elephants are poisoned with cyanide in salt pans, by poachers in Hwange National Park.

main.desc: Any molecule with a cyano group (C≡N)

events.text: The first Minotaur V rocket is launched from the Mid-Atlantic Regional Spaceport on Wallops Island, carrying NASA's LADEE spacecraft.
Hurricane Irma reached peak intensity near the Caribbean islands of Barbuda, Saint Martin, and Virgin Gorda.
The Supreme Court of India invalidated part of Section 377 of the Penal Code, thus legalising homosexuality in India.

main.desc: Highest court of jurisdiction in India

events.text: Supreme Court of India decriminalises all consensual sex among adults in private, making homosexuality legal on the Indian lands.

main.desc: Highest court of jurisdiction in India

events.text: Brazilian presidential candidate Jair Bolsonaro survives a stabbing at a campaign rally in Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais.
Liz Truss (pictured) succeeded Boris Johnson as prime minister following the July 2022 United Kingdom government crisis.

main.desc: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in 2022

events.text: Boris Johnson resigns as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, and is replaced by Liz Truss. Their meetings with Queen Elizabeth II at Balmoral Castle were the Queen's final official duties before her death two days later.

main.desc: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 2019 to 2022

links.t: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

events.text: Russo-Ukrainian war: Ukraine begins its Kharkiv counteroffensive, surprising Russian forces and retaking over 3,000 square kilometers of land, recapturing the entire Kharkiv Oblast west of the Oskil River, within the next week.

21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767 freighter operating on behalf of Amazon Air, overruns the runway upon landing at Miami International Airport, striking multiple ground vehicles, killing at least five people, and injuring five others.
Louis the Stammerer is crowned as king of West Francia by Pope John VIII.

main.desc: King of West Francia from 877 to 879

events.text: Pope Alexander III was chosen to succeed of Adrian IV in a disputed election.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1159 to 1181

events.text: Cardinal Rolando Bandinelli is elected Pope Alexander III, prompting the election of Cardinal Octaviano Monticelli as Antipope Victor IV the same day.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1159 to 1181

events.text: Third Crusade: Crusaders under Richard I of England defeated Ayyubid troops under Saladin at the Battle of Arsuf (depicted) in present-day Israel.

main.desc: 1189–1192 attempted re-conquest of the Holy Land

events.text: Third Crusade: Battle of Arsuf: Richard I of England defeats Saladin at Arsuf.

main.desc: 1189–1192 attempted re-conquest of the Holy Land

events.text: Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II lands in Acre, and starts the Sixth Crusade, which results in a peaceful restoration of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.
Guillaume de Nogaret takes Pope Boniface VIII prisoner on behalf of Philip IV of France.
Arrival of the so-called Grande Soccorso ("great relief") by Philip II of Spain to the Great Siege of Malta.
Thomas Howard, 4th Duke of Norfolk, is arrested for his role in the Ridolfi plot to assassinate Queen Elizabeth I of England and replace her with Mary, Queen of Scots.
The town of Kokkola (Swedish: Karleby) is founded by King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden.
The Treaty of Southampton makes an alliance between England and the Dutch Republic against Spain.

main.desc: 1625 alliance between England and the Dutch Republic

events.text: First English Civil War: Royalist and Parliamentarian forces clashed in the Battle of Babylon Hill, after which both sides claimed victory.

main.desc: Part of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms (1642–1646)

events.text: Chinese peasants on Formosa (now Taiwan) began a rebellion against Dutch rule which was suppressed four days later.
Around 15,000 Han farmers and militia rebel against Dutch rule on Taiwan.

Henry Every perpetrates one of the most profitable pirate raids in history with the capture of the Grand Mughal ship Ganj-i-Sawai. In response, Emperor Aurangzeb threatens to end all English trading in India.
War of the Spanish Succession: Siege of Turin ends, leading to the withdrawal of French forces from North Italy.
The treaty of Baden between the kingdom of France and the Holy Roman Empire is ratified.

main.desc: 1714 treaty between France and the Holy Roman Empire

events.text: Following the Porteous Riots, a mob storms the Tolbooth prison in Edinburgh and lynches John Porteous.
Election of Stanisław August Poniatowski as the last ruler of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

According to American colonial reports, Ezra Lee makes the world's first submarine attack in the Turtle, attempting to attach a time bomb to the hull of HMS Eagle in New York Harbor (no British records of this attack exist).

main.desc: Colonial American soldier – commander of the Turtle (1749–1821)

events.text: Anglo-French War: Having established an alliance with the United States, France invaded the Caribbean island of Dominica and captured its British fort.

main.desc: Military conflict between France and Great Britain from 1778 to 1783

events.text: American Revolutionary War: France invades Dominica in the British West Indies, before Britain is even aware of France's involvement in the war.
French invasion of Russia: The Battle of Borodino, the bloodiest battle of the Napoleonic Wars, is fought near Moscow and results in a French victory.
Carl III of Sweden–Norway is crowned king of Norway, in Trondheim.

main.desc: King of Sweden and Norway from 1818 to 1844

events.text: Pedro I declared the independence of Brazil from Portugal, establishing the Empire of Brazil (flag pictured).

main.desc: Emperor of Brazil (1822–31) and King of Portugal (1826)

events.text: Dom Pedro I declares Brazil independent from Portugal on the shores of the Ipiranga Brook in São Paulo.

main.desc: Emperor of Brazil (1822–31) and King of Portugal (1826)

events.text: The Saimaa Canal is inaugurated.
Mountain Meadows massacre: Mormon settlers slaughter most members of a peaceful emigrant wagon train.

main.desc: 1857 massacre of California-bound immigrants by Nauvoo Legion militiamen

events.text: Unification of Italy: Giuseppe Garibaldi enters Naples.
American Civil War: Union troops under Quincy A. Gillmore capture Fort Wagner in Morris Island after a seven-week siege.
American Civil War: Atlanta is evacuated on orders of Union General William Tecumseh Sherman.

main.desc: Capital and most populous city of Georgia, U.S.

events.text: In Northfield, Minnesota, Jesse James and the James–Younger Gang attempt to rob the town's bank but are driven off by armed citizens.
With Beijing occupied by foreign troops from the Eight-Nation Alliance, Qing China was forced to sign the Boxer Protocol, an unequal treaty that ended the Boxer Rebellion.
The Boxer Rebellion in Qing dynasty (modern-day China) officially ends with the signing of the Boxer Protocol.
The Ottoman Empire launches a counter-offensive against the Strandzha Commune, which dissolves.
Alberto Santos-Dumont flies his 14-bis aircraft at Bagatelle, France successfully for the first time.
Cunard Line's RMS Lusitania sets sail on her maiden voyage from Liverpool, England, to New York City.

Eugène Lefebvre crashes a new French-built Wright biplane during a test flight at Port-Aviation (often called "Juvisy Airfield") at Viry-Châtillon, south of Paris, becoming the first aviator in the world to lose his life piloting a powered heavier-than-air craft.[better source needed]
French poet Guillaume Apollinaire is arrested and put in jail on suspicion of stealing the Mona Lisa from the Louvre museum.
World War I: The Supreme War Command was established to oversee the armed forces of all the Central Powers.
US federal employees win the right to workers' compensation by Federal Employers Liability Act (39 Stat. 742; 5 U.S.C. 751).
Two newly purchased Savoia flying boats crash in the Swiss Alps en route to Finland where they were to serve with the Finnish Air Force, killing both crews.
In Atlantic City, New Jersey, the first Miss America Pageant, a two-day event, is held.

main.desc: City in Atlantic County, New Jersey, US

events.text: The Legion of Mary, the largest apostolic organization of lay people in the Catholic Church, is founded in Dublin, Ireland.

main.desc: International association of members of the Roman Catholic Church

events.text: The International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) is formed.
The first fully electronic television system is achieved by Philo Farnsworth.
Steamer Kuru capsizes and sinks on Lake Näsijärvi near Tampere in Finland. One hundred thirty-six lives are lost.

main.desc: Passenger steamship which sank in the lake Näsijärvi in Tampere, Finland (1929)

events.text: The Battle of Boquerón, the first major battle of the Chaco War, commences.
The last thylacine  died in captivity in Hobart Zoo, Australia.

main.desc: Extinct species of mammal from Australasia

events.text: The last thylacine, a carnivorous marsupial, dies alone in its cage at the Hobart Zoo in Tasmania.

main.desc: Extinct species of mammal from Australasia

events.text: Second World War: The Luftwaffe changed their strategy in the Battle of Britain and began bombing London and other cities and towns.
Romania returns Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria under the Treaty of Craiova.
World War II: The German Luftwaffe begins the Blitz, bombing London and other British cities for over 50 consecutive nights.
World War II: Japanese marines are forced to withdraw during the Battle of Milne Bay.

main.desc: Marines of the Imperial Japanese Navy

events.text: A fire at the Gulf Hotel in Houston kills 55 people.

main.desc: 1943 hotel fire in downtown Houston, Texas, United States

events.text: World War II: The German 17th Army begins its evacuation of the Kuban bridgehead (Taman Peninsula) in southern Russia and moves across the Strait of Kerch to the Crimea.

main.desc: Field army of Nazi Germany during WWII

events.text: World War II: Japanese forces on Wake Island, which they had held since December 1941, surrender to U.S. Marines.

main.desc: Pacific island administered by the United States

events.text: The Berlin Victory Parade of 1945 is held.

main.desc: Celebration of the Allies' WWII victory

events.text: Nikita Khrushchev is elected first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

main.desc: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1953 to 1964

links.t: General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union

events.text: The Pro Football Hall of Fame opens in Canton, Ohio with 17 charter members.

main.desc: Professional sports hall of fame in Canton, Ohio, U.S.

events.text: During an Indo-Pakistani War, China announces that it will reinforce its troops on the Indian border.
Vietnam War: In a follow-up to August's Operation Starlite, United States Marines and South Vietnamese forces initiate Operation Piranha on the Batangan Peninsula.
Fighting begins between Arab guerrillas and government forces in Jordan.
Vietnam Television is established.

The Torrijos–Carter Treaties between Panama and the United States on the status of the Panama Canal are signed. The United States agrees to transfer control of the canal to Panama at the end of the 20th century.

main.desc: 1977 treaties transferring the Panama Canal from the U.S. to Panama after 1999

events.text: The 300-metre (980 ft) tall CKVR-DT transmission tower in Barrie, Ontario, Canada, is hit by a light aircraft in a fog, causing it to collapse. All aboard the aircraft are killed.

While walking across Waterloo Bridge in London, Bulgarian dissident Georgi Markov is assassinated by Bulgarian secret police agent Francesco Gullino by means of a ricin pellet fired from a specially designed umbrella.
The Chrysler Corporation asks the United States government for US$1.5 billion to avoid bankruptcy.
An explosion on board a Maltese patrol boat that was disposing of illegal fireworks at sea off Gozo killed seven soldiers and policemen.
An explosion on board a Maltese patrol boat disposing of illegal fireworks at sea off Gozo kills seven soldiers and policemen.
Desmond Tutu became the first black leader of the Anglican Church of Southern Africa.

main.desc: South African bishop and anti-apartheid activist (1931–2021)

events.text: Desmond Tutu becomes the first black man to lead the Anglican Diocese of Cape Town.

main.desc: South African bishop and anti-apartheid activist (1931–2021)

events.text: Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet survives an assassination attempt by the FPMR; five of Pinochet's bodyguards are killed.
Space Shuttle Endeavour is launched on STS-69, the second flight of the Wake Shield Facility.
American rapper Tupac Shakur was fatally shot in Paradise, Nevada, dying six days later.
Maiden flight of the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor.

main.desc: First occasion in which an aircraft or rocket leaves the ground under its own power

events.text: Three weeks after an earthquake struck northwestern Turkey, a second earthquake struck Athens, causing Greece and Turkey to initiate "earthquake diplomacy".
The 6.0 Mw Athens earthquake affects the area with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), killing 143, injuring 800–1,600, and leaving 50,000 homeless.
Hurricane Ivan made landfall on Grenada, devastating at least 85 per cent of buildings on the island.
Egypt holds its first-ever multi-party presidential election.
The United States government takes control of the two largest mortgage financing companies in the US, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

main.t: Federal takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac
main.desc: Action by the U.S. Treasury to lessen the subprime mortgage crisis

events.text: A Chinese fishing trawler operating in disputed waters collided with Japan Coast Guard patrol boats near the Senkaku Islands, sparking a major diplomatic dispute between the two countries.

main.desc: Commercial vessel designed to operate fishing trawls

events.text: A Chinese fishing trawler collides with two Japanese Coast Guard patrol boats in disputed waters near the Senkaku Islands.

main.desc: Diplomatic dispute between Japan and China

events.text: Yak-Service Flight 9633, carrying the players and coaching staff of the ice hockey team Lokomotiv Yaroslavl, crashed on take-off near Yaroslavl, Russia, resulting in the deaths of 44 of the 45 people on board.
The Lokomotiv Yaroslavl plane crash in Russia kills 43 people, including nearly the entire roster of the Lokomotiv Yaroslavl Kontinental Hockey League team.
Canada officially cuts diplomatic ties with Iran by closing its embassy in Tehran and orders the expulsion of Iranian diplomats from Ottawa, over nuclear plans and purported human rights abuses.
The 8.2 Mw 2017 Chiapas earthquake strikes southern Mexico, killing at least 60 people.

main.desc: 8.2 Mw earthquake and tsunami off of Mexico and Guatemala

events.text: Ukrainian filmmaker Oleg Sentsov and 66 others are released in a prisoner exchange between Ukraine and Russia.
Bitcoin becomes legal tender in El Salvador.
The National Unity Government of Myanmar declares a people's defensive war against the military junta during the Myanmar civil war.
The funeral of Augustus takes place. His body is cremated and placed in his mausoleum.

main.desc: Second decade of the first century AD

events.text: After the capture of Herod's Palace the previous day, a Roman army under Titus secures and plunders the city of Jerusalem.
Li Yuan defeated a Sui army at the Battle of Huoyi, opening the path to his capture of the Chinese imperial capital Chang'an and the eventual establishment of the Tang dynasty.
Battle of Huoyi: Li Yuan defeats a Sui dynasty army, opening the path to his capture of the imperial capital Chang'an and the eventual establishment of the Tang dynasty.
Theodoric was elected by opponents of Pope Paschal II, following the death of Antipope Clement III.
Election of Antipope Theodoric.
Philip of Swabia, Prince of Hohenstaufen, is crowned King of Germany (King of the Romans).
Pope Innocent IV canonises Stanislaus of Szczepanów, who was killed by King Bolesław II.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1243 to 1254

events.text: The Statute of Kalisz, guaranteeing Jews safety and personal liberties and giving battei din jurisdiction over Jewish matters, is promulgated by Bolesław the Pious, Duke of Greater Poland.

main.desc: 1264 decree by the Duke of Greater Poland

events.text: Election of Pope John XXI following the sudden death of pope Hadrian V in the previous month. This was the third papal election that year as both predecessors of Pope John XXI died in the same year.

main.desc: Election of Catholic Pope John XXI

events.text: Stefan Dušan declares himself king of Serbia.
The Battle of Adramyttion begins in which a Christian naval league defeats a Turkish fleet in several encounters.
Battle of Kulikovo: Russian forces defeat a mixed army of Tatars and Mongols, stopping their advance.

main.desc: Battle between Russian principalities and Mongol forces

events.text: Michelangelo's David is unveiled in Piazza della Signoria in Florence.
Battle of Orsha: In one of the biggest battles of the century, Lithuanians and Poles defeat the Russian army.

main.desc: Part of the fourth Muscovite–Lithuanian War (1514)

events.text: Magellan–Elcano circumnavigation: Victoria arrives at Seville, completing the first circumnavigation.
St. Augustine, Florida, the oldest continuously occupied settlement of European origin in the contiguous United States, was founded by Spanish admiral Pedro Menéndez de Avilés.
St. Augustine, Florida is founded by Spanish admiral and Florida's first governor, Pedro Menéndez de Avilés.
Ottoman–Habsburg wars: Ottoman forces led by Suleiman the Magnificent captured the fortress of Szigetvár in Hungary, but were forced to end their campaign to take Vienna.
Warsaw falls without resistance to a small force under the command of Charles X Gustav of Sweden during The Deluge, making it the first time the city is captured by a foreign army.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Poland

events.text: J. S. Bach led the first performance of Geist und Seele wird verwirret, a solo cantata for alto voice.

links.t: Geist und Seele wird verwirret, BWV 35

events.text: J. S. Bach leads the first performance of Geist und Seele wird verwirret, BWV 35, a solo cantata for alto voice.

links.t: Geist und Seele wird verwirret, BWV 35

events.text: A barn fire during a puppet show in the village of Burwell in Cambridgeshire, England kills 78 people, many of whom are children.

French and Indian War: Despite being ambushed at the start of the Battle of Lake George, British colonial troops and their Mohawk allies were able to defeat French and Canadien troops and their Indian allies.

main.desc: North American theater of the Seven Years' War

events.text: French and Indian War: Battle of Lake George.

main.desc: North American theater of the Seven Years' War

events.text: French and Indian War: Kittanning Expedition.

main.desc: 1756 expedition of the French and Indian War

events.text: French and Indian War: French surrender Montreal to the British, completing the latter's conquest of New France.
Marriage of King George III of the United Kingdom to Duchess Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz.

main.desc: King of Great Britain and Ireland from 1760 to 1820

events.text: Maltese priests discontented with the Order of Saint John led an uprising that was quickly suppressed by the Order.
The unsuccessful Rising of the Priests in Malta.

main.desc: 1775 Maltese uprising against the Knights Hospitaller

events.text: American Revolutionary War: The Battle of Eutaw Springs in South Carolina, the war's last significant battle in the Southern theater, ends in a narrow British tactical victory.

links.t: Southern theater of the American Revolutionary War

events.text: French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of Hondschoote.
French Revolutionary Wars: The French defeated Austrian forces in Bassano, Venetia, Italy.
French Revolutionary Wars: Led by Napoleon, French forces defeated the Austrians at the Battle of Bassano in Veneto, Italy.
French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of Bassano: French forces defeat Austrian troops at Bassano del Grappa.

main.desc: 1796 battle during the War of the First Coalition

events.text: The Treaty of Paris is signed ending the French military occupation of Prussia.
The Tonquin sets sail from New York Harbor with 33 employees of John Jacob Astor's newly created Pacific Fur Company on board.
At the final stage of the Peninsular War, British-Portuguese troops capture the town of Donostia (now San Sebastián), resulting in a rampage and eventual destruction of the town.
1819 Balloon riot occurred at Vauxhall Garden in Philadelphia, PA and resulted in the destruction of the amusement park.
The Russian Empire suppressed the November Uprising in Poland with the capture of Warsaw after a two-day assault.
William IV and Adelaide of Saxe-Meiningen were crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

main.desc: King of the United Kingdom from 1830 to 1837

links.t: Coronation of William IV and Adelaide
United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

events.text: William IV and Adelaide of Saxe-Meiningen are crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

main.desc: King of the United Kingdom from 1830 to 1837

events.text: November uprising: The Battle of Warsaw effectively ends the Polish insurrection.

main.desc: Anti-Russian uprising in the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth (1830–31)

events.text: Crimean War: The French assault the tower of Malakoff, leading to the capture of Sevastopol.

main.desc: Tenth conflict of the Russo-Turkish wars (1853–1856)

events.text: The paddle steamer Lady Elgin (pictured) was rammed by a schooner on Lake Michigan and sank, resulting in the loss of about 300 lives.

main.desc: Steam-powered vessel propelled by paddle wheels

events.text: The steamship PS Lady Elgin sinks on Lake Michigan, with the loss of around 300 lives.
Millennium of Russia monument is unveiled in Novgorod.

main.desc: Bronze monument in Novgorod Oblast, Russia

events.text: American Civil War: In the Second Battle of Sabine Pass, a small Confederate force thwarts a Union invasion of Texas.

The Northern Pacific Railway (reporting mark NP) was completed in a ceremony at Gold Creek, Montana. Former president Ulysses S. Grant drove in the final "golden spike" in an event attended by rail and political luminaries.

main.desc: Defunct transcontinental railroad company in the northwest United States (1864-1970)

events.text: Isaac Peral's submarine is first tested.
The Great Herding (Spanish: El Gran Arreo) begins with thousands of sheep being herded from the Argentine outpost of Fortín Conesa to Santa Cruz near the Strait of Magellan.
In London, the body of Jack the Ripper's second murder victim, Annie Chapman, is found.
In England, the first six Football League matches are played.
The Pledge of Allegiance is first recited.

main.desc: Loyalty oath to the flag and republic of the U.S.

events.text: Seven hundred Greek civilians, 17 British guards and the British Consul of Crete are killed by a Turkish mob.

The Great Galveston hurricane, the deadliest natural disaster in U.S. history, struck Galveston, Texas, with estimated winds of 135 miles per hour (215 km/h) at landfall, killing at least 6,000 people.

links.t: List of disasters in the United States by death toll

events.text: Galveston hurricane: A powerful hurricane hits Galveston, Texas killing about 8,000 people.
The 7.2 Mw Calabria earthquake shakes southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing between 557 and 2,500 people.
Gertrude Stein meets her life partner and muse, Alice B. Toklas in Paris.
World War I: Private Thomas Highgate becomes the first British soldier to be executed for desertion during the war.

In a bid to prove that women were capable of serving as military dispatch riders, Augusta and Adeline Van Buren arrive in Los Angeles, completing a 60-day, 5,500 mile cross-country trip on motorcycles.
In Atlantic City, New Jersey, Margaret Gorman (pictured) was crowned the "Golden Mermaid", the forerunner to the Miss America pageant.

main.desc: City in Atlantic County, New Jersey, US

events.text: Margaret Gorman, a 16-year-old, wins the Atlantic City Pageant's Golden Mermaid trophy; pageant officials later dubbed her the first Miss America.
Honda Point disaster: Nine US Navy destroyers run aground off the California coast. Seven are lost, and twenty-three sailors killed.

main.desc: Largest peacetime loss of U.S. Navy ships

events.text: Rif War: Spanish forces including troops from the Foreign Legion under Colonel Francisco Franco landing at Al Hoceima, Morocco.

main.desc: 1921–1926 war between Spain and Riffian tribes of Morocco

events.text: Germany is admitted to the League of Nations.
Ghazi bin Faisal became King of Iraq.
Off the New Jersey coast, a fire aboard the passenger liner SS Morro Castle kills 137 people.
Huey Long, a U.S. senator, was shot in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, dying two days later.
US Senator from Louisiana Huey Long is fatally shot in the Louisiana State Capitol building.

Opposed to António de Oliveira Salazar's support of the Nationalists in the Spanish Civil War, the crews of the Portuguese Navy ships NRP Afonso de Albuquerque and NRP Dão mutinied while anchored in the harbour of Lisbon.
World War II: German forces begin the Siege of Leningrad.
World War II: The Armistice of Cassibile is proclaimed by radio. OB Süd immediately implements plans to disarm the Italian forces.

main.desc: 1943 armistice ending the hostilities between Italy and the Allies

events.text: World War II: London is hit by a V-2 rocket for the first time.
The division of Korea begins when United States troops arrive to partition the southern part of Korea in response to Soviet troops occupying the northern part of the peninsula a month earlier.

main.desc: Separation of North and South Korea

events.text: A referendum abolishes the monarchy in Bulgaria.
The flag of North Korea is adopted with the passing of the country's first constitution by the Supreme People's Assembly.
The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation makes its first televised broadcast on the second escape of the Boyd Gang.
Eight nations signed a collective-defense treaty in Manila to create the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (flag pictured), modelled on NATO.
The Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO) is established.
In Huntsville, Alabama, US President Dwight D. Eisenhower formally dedicates the Marshall Space Flight Center (NASA had already activated the facility on July 1).
Last run of the famous Pines Express over the Somerset and Dorset Railway line (UK) fittingly using the last steam locomotive built by British Railways, BR Standard Class 9F 92220 Evening Star.

main.desc: Former passenger train between Manchester and Bournemouth, England (1910-67)

events.text: Queen Elizabeth II opened the Severn Bridge, suggesting that it marked the dawn of a new economic era for South Wales.

main.desc: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1952 to 2022

events.text: The science fiction show Star Trek made its American premiere with "The Man Trap", launching a media franchise that has since created a cult phenomenon and has influenced the design of many current technologies.
Queen Elizabeth II opened the Severn Bridge (pictured), linking South Gloucestershire in England and Monmouthshire in Wales.

main.desc: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1952 to 2022

events.text: The landmark American science fiction television series Star Trek premieres with its first-aired episode, "The Man Trap".
Trans International Airlines Flight 863 crashes during takeoff from John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City, killing all 11 aboard.
In Washington, D.C., the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts is inaugurated, with the opening feature being the premiere of Leonard Bernstein's Mass.

main.desc: National cultural center of the United States

events.text: World Airways Flight 802 crashes into Mount Dutton in King Cove, Alaska, killing six people.
Watergate scandal: U.S. president Gerald Ford gave his recently resigned predecessor Richard Nixon a controversial full and unconditional pardon for any crimes he committed while in office.
Watergate scandal: US President Gerald Ford signs the pardon of Richard Nixon for any crimes Nixon may have committed while in office.

Gays in the military: US Air Force Tech Sergeant Leonard Matlovich, a decorated veteran of the Vietnam War, appears in his Air Force uniform on the cover of Time magazine with the headline "I Am A Homosexual". He is given a general discharge, later upgraded to honorable.
Black Friday, a massacre by soldiers against protesters in Tehran, results in 88 deaths, it marks the beginning of the end of the monarchy in Iran.

main.desc: Mass shooting of protesters in Pahlavi Iran on 8 September 1978

events.text: Nicholas Daniloff, a correspondent for U.S. News & World Report, is indicted on charges of espionage by the Soviet Union.
Yellowstone National Park is closed for the first time in U.S. history due to ongoing fires.

main.desc: Natural event in Yellowstone National Park, United States

events.text: Partnair Flight 394 dives into the North Sea, killing 55 people. The investigation showed that the tail of the plane vibrated loose in flight due to sub-standard connecting bolts that had been fraudulently sold as aircraft-grade.

main.desc: 1989 aviation accident in the North Sea

events.text: At the Tailhook Association symposium in Las Vegas, U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aviators were alleged to have sexually assaulted 90 persons.
USAir Flight 427 crashed on approach to Pittsburgh International Airport, resulting in 132 deaths and the longest accident investigation in the history of the National Transportation Safety Board.

USAir Flight 427, on approach to Pittsburgh International Airport, suddenly crashes in clear weather killing all 132 aboard, resulting in the most extensive aviation investigation in world history and altering manufacturing practices in the industry.
Construction began on the Dhammakaya Cetiya, a giant stupa at the Wat Phra Dhammakaya, a Buddhist temple in Pathum Thani, Thailand.

main.desc: History of a Thai Buddhist temple

events.text: NASA launches Space Shuttle Atlantis on STS-106 to resupply the International Space Station.
NASA's uncrewed spacecraft Genesis crash-lands when its parachute fails to open.
Two Ilyushin Il-76 aircraft from EMERCOM land at a disaster aid staging area at Little Rock Air Force Base; the first time Russia has flown such a mission to North America.

main.desc: Russian heavy four-engined military transport jet aircraft

events.text: NASA launches OSIRIS-REx, its first asteroid sample return mission. The probe visited 101955 Bennu and returned with samples in September 2023.

Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) announce the beginning of the Deir ez-Zor campaign, with the stated aim of eliminating the Islamic State (IS) from all areas north and east of the Euphrates.

main.desc: 1561 conference between Catholics and Protestants (Huguenots) in France

main.desc: Conflict between the Ottoman Empire and the Holy League

main.desc: Convention of delegates that became the governing body of the United States (1774–1789)

Alexander I of Russia confirms the privileges of Baltic provinces.
John Herschel takes the first glass plate photograph.
Possible start of the Great Famine of Ireland.

California is admitted as the thirty-first U.S. state.

main.desc: Tenth conflict of the Russo-Turkish wars (1853–1856)

A British force repels an Egyptian force led by Ahmed Urabi in the battle of Qassasin during the Anglo-Egyptian War.

Amalthea becomes the last moon to be discovered without the use of photography.

The Greco-Turkish War effectively ends with Turkish victory over the Greeks in Smyrna.

main.desc: Conflict between the Kingdom of Greece and the Turkish National Movement

events.text: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder of the Republic of Turkey, founds the Republican People's Party.
Hanapepe massacre occurs on Kauai, Hawaii.
Yleisradio (YLE), the Finnish national public broadcasting company, begins its broadcasts.

The crews of Portuguese Navy frigate NRP Afonso de Albuquerque and destroyer Dão mutiny against the Salazar dictatorship's support of General Franco's coup and declare their solidarity with the Spanish Republic.

main.desc: Naval branch of the Portuguese Armed Forces

Burmese national hero U Ottama dies in prison after a hunger strike to protest Britain's colonial government.

main.desc: Buddhist monk and leader of the Burmese independence movement

events.text: George Stibitz pioneers the first remote operation of a computer.

main.desc: American inventor of the digital computer

events.text: Treznea Massacre in Transylvania.

main.desc: Military coalition in World War II

Kim Il Sung is appointed as premier of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea). This is celebrated annually as its national holiday.

main.desc: Earthquake of the coast of Algeria

main.desc: Earthquake of the coast of Algeria

events.text: Elvis Presley appears on The Ed Sullivan Show for the first time.
U.S. president Dwight D. Eisenhower signed the Civil Rights Act of 1957, the first civil rights bill since Reconstruction.

main.desc: World War II general, U.S. president from 1953 to 1961

events.text: French president Charles de Gaulle delivered his "speech to the German youth" to 20,000 people in the courtyard of Ludwigsburg Palace (pictured).

main.t: United States Department of Housing and Urban Development

main.t: National Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act

Allegheny Airlines Flight 863 collides in mid-air with a Piper PA-28 Cherokee over Moral Township, Shelby County, Indiana, killing all 83 people on board both aircraft.
A British airliner is hijacked by the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine and flown to Dawson's Field in Jordan.

main.t: Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine

events.text: Imagine, the second solo album by John Lennon (pictured), was released.
The four-day Attica Prison riot begins, eventually resulting in 39 dead, most killed by state troopers retaking the prison.

In Kentucky's Mammoth Cave National Park, a Cave Research Foundation exploration and mapping team discovers a link between the Mammoth and Flint Ridge cave systems, making it the longest known cave passageway in the world.
Two Aeroflot flights collide in mid-air over Anapa, Soviet Union, killing 70.
Vietnam Airlines Flight 831 crashes in Khu Khot, Thailand, while on approach to Don Muang International Airport, killing 76.
Batticaloa massacre: Massacre of 184 Tamil civilians by the Sri Lankan Army in Batticaloa District.

main.desc: Killing of Tamil refugees by the Sri Lankan Army

main.desc: Efforts to resolve the Israeli–Palestinian conflict

The first banknotes of the Portrait Series of the Singapore dollar were introduced by the Board of Commissioners of Currency.
Two al-Qaeda attackers assassinated Ahmad Shah Massoud, a pivotal Afghan resistance leader, two days before the September 11 attacks in the United States.
Ahmad Shah Massoud, leader of the Northern Alliance, is assassinated in Afghanistan by two al-Qaeda assassins who claimed to be Arab journalists wanting an interview.

events.text: The Dubai Metro, the first urban train network in the Arabian Peninsula, is ceremonially inaugurated.
A natural-gas pipeline in San Bruno, California, exploded and "shot a fireball more than 1,000 feet (300 m) in the air", killing eight people.
The Indian space agency puts into orbit its heaviest foreign satellite yet, in a streak of 21 consecutive successful PSLV launches.

main.desc: Indian national space and aeronautics agency

events.text: A wave of attacks kills more than 100 people and injure 350 others across Iraq.

The album Songs of Innocence by U2 is digitally released at no charge to all customers of the iTunes Music Store, appearing automatically in the "purchased" section of over 500 million users worldwide.

Six people are killed when Israel carries out an airstrike on Doha in a failed attempt to decapitate the Hamas leadership.
Several Russian drones incur on Polish airspace and are subsequently shot down, marking the first time a NATO member has engaged Russian military assets.

John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy is assassinated by adherents of the Dauphin, the future Charles VII of France.

Fifty-five Christians are executed in Nagasaki during the Great Genna Martyrdom.

The treaty of Tangier ends the Franco-Moroccan War, which Morocco lost, and forces it to recognise the French possessions in Algeria.
John Doubleday completed a "masterly" restoration of the Portland Vase, which had been smashed into hundreds of pieces seven months prior.
Elias Howe is granted a patent for the sewing machine.
George Mary Searle discovered the asteroid 55 Pandora (pictured) from the Dudley Observatory near Albany, New York; it was his only asteroid discovery.
George Mary Searle discovers the asteroid 55 Pandora.

main.desc: Multi-party war in the former Russian Empire (1917–1922)

The people of Gibraltar vote to remain a British dependency rather than becoming part of Spain.

Guinea-Bissau gains independence from Portugal.

Hamida Djandoubi, convicted of torture and murder, is the last person to be executed by guillotine in France.

Switzerland, traditionally a neutral country, becomes a full member of the United Nations.
Former Prime Minister of Pakistan Nawaz Sharif returns to Pakistan after seven years in exile, following a military coup in October 1999.
The Large Hadron Collider at CERN, described as the biggest scientific experiment in history, is powered up in Geneva, Switzerland.

Polaris Dawn, the first private crewed spaceflight to involve a spacewalk, is launched from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

South Africa grants independence to the "homeland" of Venda (not recognised outside South Africa).
Spantax Flight 995 crashes at Málaga Airport during a rejected takeoff, killing 50 of the 394 people on board.

Largest anti-Apartheid march in South Africa, led by Desmond Tutu.

main.desc: South African system of racial segregation

events.text: Nirvana released their third and final studio album, In Utero, which went on to sell more than 15 million copies.

Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin shakes hands with Palestine Liberation Organization chairman Yasser Arafat at the White House after signing the Oslo Accords granting limited Palestinian autonomy.

main.desc: Air warfare branch of the German military

events.text: Civilian aircraft traffic resumes in the United States after the September 11 attacks.
A software bug caused a simulated pandemic in the online video game World of Warcraft, serving as a model for epidemiologists to understand how human interaction influences disease outbreaks.

main.desc: Virtual epidemic in World of Warcraft

events.text: The Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples is adopted by the United Nations General Assembly.

main.t: Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples
main.desc: Declaration adopted in 2007 by the United Nations General Assembly

events.text: The McLaren F1 team are found guilty of possessing confidential information from the Ferrari team, fined $100 million, and excluded from the constructors' championship standings.
Five bomb blasts took place in Delhi, India, killing at least 20 people as part of a series of attacks perpetrated by the Indian Mujahideen.

main.desc: Megacity and union territory of India

events.text: Taliban insurgents attack the United States consulate in Herat, Afghanistan, with two members of the Afghan National Police reported dead and about 20 civilians injured.

Domitian became Emperor of the Roman Empire upon the death of his brother Titus.

Seljuk atabeg Imad al-Din Zengi of Mosul is assassinated by a slave and succeeded by his quarrelling sons.

main.desc: Conflict between the Minamoto and Taira clans of feudal Japan (1180–1185)

The first recorded instance of the Catholic practice of perpetual Eucharistic adoration formally begins in Avignon, France.

events.text: Bishop Gore School, one of the oldest schools in Wales, is founded.

main.desc: Conflict between the Republic of Venice and the Ottoman Empire (1684–1698)

events.text: George Frideric Handel completes his oratorio Messiah.
Under the terms of the Calendar (New Style) Act 1750, the British Empire adopted the Gregorian calendar, skipping 11 days of the month.

main.desc: British statute adopting the Gregorian calendar

Seneca warriors defeat British forces at the Battle of Devil's Hole during Pontiac's War.

main.desc: Haudenosaunee group of the Eastern Woodlands of North America

Jang Bahadur and his brothers massacre about 40 members of the Nepalese palace court.

main.desc: Founder of the Rana dynasty in Nepal

main.desc: President of the United States from 1901 to 1909

main.desc: President of the United States from 1897 to 1901

events.text: Russian Premier Pyotr Stolypin is shot by Dmitry Bogrov while attending a performance of Rimsky-Korsakov's The Tale of Tsar Saltan at the Kiev Opera House, in the presence of Tsar Nicholas II.

main.desc: Prime Minister of the Russian Empire from 1906 to 1911

main.desc: E-class submarine of the Royal Australian Navy

events.text: The Russian Empire is formally replaced by the Russian Republic.
Raoul Villain, who assassinated the French Socialist Jean Jaurès, is himself killed by Spanish Republicans in Ibiza.

main.desc: French nationalist; assassinator of French socialist leader Jean Jaurès in 1914

Hungarian forces massacred at least 150 ethnic Romanians in Ip, Transylvania, following rumors that Romanians were responsible for the deaths of two soldiers.

main.desc: 1940 massacre in Ip, Kingdom of Hungary

main.desc: 1940 massacre in Ip, Kingdom of Hungary

main.desc: City and municipality in Limburg, Netherlands

main.desc: Land service branch of the Indian Armed Forces

The first two German post-war rockets, designed by the German engineer Ernst Mohr, reach the upper atmosphere.

main.desc: Sounding rocket developed in Germany in the 1950s

events.text: The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is founded.
Congo Crisis: Mobutu Sese Seko seizes power in a military coup, suspending parliament and the constitution.
The first American saint, Elizabeth Ann Seton, is canonized by Pope Paul VI.

main.desc: American Roman Catholic educator and saint (1774–1821)
