main.t: List of heads of state of Afghanistan

events.text: President-elect of Lebanon Bachir Gemayel is assassinated.
Joe Kittinger becomes the first person to fly a gas balloon alone across the Atlantic Ocean.
Penang Bridge, the longest bridge in Malaysia, connecting the island of Penang to the mainland, opens to traffic.

main.desc: Road bridge connecting Penang Island with the Malay Peninsula

events.text: Typhoon Sarah dissipated after causing extensive damage along an erratic path across the Western Pacific, killing 71 in Taiwan, the Philippines, and the Gotō Islands.
The Standard Gravure shooting where Joseph T. Wesbecker, a 47-year-old pressman, killed eight people and injured 12 people at his former workplace, Standard Gravure, before committing suicide.
The Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina declared the breakaway Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia to be unconstitutional.

main.desc: Unrecognized proto-state in the Balkans (1991–1996); now part of Bosnia and Herzegovina

events.text: The Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina declares the breakaway Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia to be illegal.
Lufthansa Flight 2904, an Airbus A320, crashes into an embankment after overshooting the runway at Okęcie International Airport (now Warsaw Chopin Airport), killing two people.

main.desc: 1993 passenger plane crash in Warsaw, Poland

events.text: The rest of the Major League Baseball season is canceled because of a strike.
Eighty-one killed as five bogies of the Ahmedabad–Howrah Express plunge into a river in Bilaspur district of Madhya Pradesh, India.
Telecommunications companies MCI Communications and WorldCom complete their $37 billion merger to form MCI WorldCom.
Kiribati, Nauru and Tonga join the United Nations.

main.desc: Island country in the central Pacific

events.text: Microsoft releases Windows Me.

Historic National Prayer Service held at Washington National Cathedral for victims of the September 11 attacks. A similar service is held in Canada on Parliament Hill, the largest vigil ever held in the nation's capital.
Total Linhas Aéreas Flight 5561 crashes near Paranapanema, Brazil, killing both pilots on board.
President Kumba Ialá (pictured) of Guinea-Bissau was deposed in a bloodless military coup.
In a referendum, Estonia approves joining the European Union.
Bissau-Guinean President Kumba Ialá is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by General Veríssimo Correia Seabra.

Prelude to the 2008 financial crisis: Northern Rock bank experiences the first bank run in the United Kingdom in 150 years.
Aeroflot Flight 821, a Boeing 737-500, crashes into a section of the Trans-Siberian Railway while on approach to Perm International Airport, in Perm, Russia, killing all 88 people on board.

The first observation of gravitational waves is made, announced by the LIGO and Virgo collaborations on 11 February 2016.
Drone attacks on major processing facilities at Abqaiq and Khurais forced Saudi Arabia to cut more than half of its oil production.

main.desc: 2019 drone attack on Saudi oil processing facilities

events.text: Yemen's Houthi rebels claim responsibility for an attack on Saudi Arabian oil facilities.

Death of Queen Elizabeth II: The Queen's coffin is taken from Buckingham Palace, placed on a gun carriage of The King's Troop Royal Horse Artillery and moved in a procession to Westminster Hall for her lying in state over the next four days with the queue of mourners stretching for miles along the River Thames.

main.t: Death and state funeral of Elizabeth II

events.text: The Byzantine army under Belisarius enters Carthage following their victory over the Vandals at Ad Decimum.

main.desc: Land branch of the armed forces of the Byzantine Empire

events.text: Consecration of pope Boniface IV following his approval by the Byzantine emperor.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 608 to 615

events.text: Major Fatimid victory over the Byzantine Empire at the Battle of the Orontes.
Gilles de Rais, one of the earliest known serial killers, is taken into custody upon an accusation brought against him by  Jean de Malestroit, Bishop of Nantes.

main.desc: Conquest of the island of Lesbos by the Ottoman Empire

events.text: Appearance of the miraculous portrait of Saint Dominic in Soriano in Soriano Calabro, Calabria, Italy; commemorated as a feast day by the Roman Catholic Church 1644–1912.
Departing from Vlissingen, ex-Holy Roman Emperor Charles V returns to Spain.
Seven Years' War: Battle of Signal Hill.

main.desc: Executive department of the U.S. federal government

links.t: Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen

links.t: Low Countries theatre of the War of the First Coalition

Britain seizes the Dutch Cape Colony in southern Africa to prevent its use by the Batavian Republic.

main.desc: Field army of the French Imperial Army

events.text: War of 1812: A second supply train sent to relieve Fort Harrison is ambushed in the Attack at the Narrows.
Followers of the Eight Trigram Sect loyal to Lin Qing attack the Forbidden City in a failed attempt to oust the Jiaqing Emperor of the Qing dynasty.

main.desc: Network of Chinese folk religious sects

events.text: HMS Whiting runs aground on the Doom Bar.
Constitutionalist revolution in Lisbon, Portugal.
The Province of Guatemala proclaimed the independence of Central America from the Spanish Empire.

main.t: Act of Independence of Central America
main.desc: 1821 declaration of Guatemalan independence from the Spanish Empire

links.t: Act of Independence of Central America

American Civil War: Confederate forces capture Harpers Ferry, Virginia.

main.desc: Early 20th-century revolt against traditional Chinese values

World War I: Allied troops break through the Bulgarian defenses on the Macedonian front.

main.desc: 1918 battle in the Balkans Campaign of World War I

main.desc: Nazi Germany antisemitic and racist laws

Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill meet in Quebec as part of the Octagon Conference to discuss strategy.

main.desc: World War II battle in the Pacific theater

main.desc: Land service branch of the Indian Armed Forces

main.desc: President of the United States from 1963 to 1969

The Parsons Green bombing takes place in London.

Armenian champion swimmer Shavarsh Karapetyan saves 20 people from a trolleybus that had fallen into a Yerevan reservoir.

The cruise ferry MS Estonia sinks in the Baltic Sea, killing 852 people.

Tegucigalpa, capital city of Honduras, is claimed by the Spaniards.

A Haitian coup d'état occurs.

Archaeologists and volunteers began excavation of the remains of Fort Tanjong Katong in Singapore.
